goal: Issue #716 — constellation: work_id-with-slash parsing breaks run_crew.py + verify_agent_feedback.py under the nested Commander-under-Admiral convention (epic-<N>/<issue>). Resolve, to shared understanding, what is actually broken, where it is maintained, and what the bounded fix is. PLANNING ONLY: the engagement stops after the Commander plan step.

questions.question: Where are run_crew.py and verify_agent_feedback.py canonically maintained, and does f1Brainz need any change at all?
questions.resolution: Canonical home is the constellation-skills repo at C:/Programs/constellation-skills/scripts/. The ~/.claude/skills/constellation-*/scripts/ copies are install output. f1Brainz needs no source change — it only invokes the installed copies by absolute path from spine check-commands.

questions.question: Do both named defects still reproduce against canonical HEAD, and do they fail loudly or silently?
questions.resolution: Both reproduce, and both fail MISLEADINGLY rather than loudly. load_registry_for_resume returns [] (a missing registry file is an empty registry), so a wrong-work-id lookup is indistinguishable from 'no crews yet'. _current_run_archive_dirs returns [] against a real package, surfacing as 'no archived run package found' — blaming the operator. Regression tests must therefore assert the POSITIVE match, not merely that an error is raised.
questions.code_evidence: .agent-work/issue-716/evidence/repro_716.py (run 2026-08-01, output captured in the mission frame); run_crew.py:106-113 (load_registry), :933-940 (load_registry_for_resume); verify_agent_feedback.py:72-80, :129-136

questions.question: Is the crew session-name grammar unambiguously parseable when work_id contains '/'?
questions.resolution: Yes, from the RIGHT. The last three segments are fixed (gate, role, attempt-<n>), so work_id = '/'.join(parts[1:-3]). For a slashless work_id this is byte-identical to today's parts[1], so the change is strictly additive.
questions.code_evidence: run_crew.py:83-88 (session_name), :99-103 (run_log_paths uses gate/role verbatim as filename stems, so neither can contain '/'), :770-771 (--gate/--role are single CLI tokens)

questions.question: What archive layout does a slashed work_id actually produce on disk today?
questions.resolution: Nested. No script performs the move; the commander spine's prose imperative interpolates '<date>-<work-id>', which for 'epic-659/665' yields archive/2026-07-25-epic-659/665/ — two levels. The existing single-level path.name rule is exactly the N=1 case of a relative-path rule.
questions.code_evidence: templates/COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json archive imperative ('Move .agent-work/<work-id>/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-<work-id>/'); verify_agent_feedback.py:72-80 (iterdir + path.name); repro_716.py output

questions.question: Fix by changing the archive NAMING CONVENTION (flatten '/' in the dir name) or by making the MATCHER handle the nested layout?
questions.resolution: Option A — generalize the matcher; leave the '<date>-<work-id>' convention untouched. Smaller blast radius (one helper + one call site vs. rewriting the archive sentence in three spine templates and orphaning existing archives); it removes a rule an agent must remember rather than adding one; and the N=1 case stays bit-identical. The matcher will additionally tolerate a flattened name so a future move to B costs nothing.

questions.question: How does a NEW shared module reach every installed skill that bundles the two scripts?
questions.resolution: Only via install_constellation.py, and it needs an explicit edit or the helper silently fails to install — the exact gauge_reader.py drift the installer's own comment documents. The right lever is SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS + expand_script_bundle, which propagates to commander, commander-delegated, admiral and explorer without hand-editing four bundles. GAP: the pinning test only parses checklist_engine.py for the 'parent / "x.py"' idiom, so a plain import is invisible to it.

questions.question: What is the governing evidence surface for a change in the constellation-skills repo?
questions.resolution: C:/Programs/constellation-skills/tests/ — unittest modules run under pytest, one file per script. f1Brainz's ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT evidence table does not bind this change. Existing coverage is slashless-only, which is why the defect shipped; tests/test_work_id.py is the natural home for the shared helper, mirroring test_agent_work_root.py.

questions.question: Does the shared helper get its own module, or extend an existing one?
questions.resolution: A new scripts/work_id.py. agent_work_root.py has one job (durable-root resolution) and is not bundled to explorer, which does carry run_crew.py; folding the parser in would either under-install the helper or drag agent_work_root.py into explorer's bundle for an unrelated reason. A separate module gives the two call sites one seam and a clean deletion test.
